About us

New Zealand Blood Service (NZBS) was created on 1 July 1998 to provide the people of New Zealand with safe, appropriate and timely access to blood and tissue products and related services to meet their health needs. NZBS takes the responsibility for the development of an integrated national blood transfusion process from the collection of blood from volunteer donors to the transfusion of blood products within the hospital environment - a ‘vein to vein’ transfusion service. Every minute, every day, someone in New Zealand needs blood. At NZBS, everything we do revolves around finding the right match. Our role is to pair donors with recipients – not only for blood products and stem cells, but also in many areas of organ and tissue donation and transplantation.     “Without the generosity and commitment of plasma donors and everyone at New Zealand Blood Service, my life and that of many others would be fundamentally different. They truly have had a life changing impact on me.” In 2019, Clive Phillips was diagnosed with Multifocal Motor Neuropathy (MMN), an autoimmune condition that causes progressive muscle weakness and loss of motor function. A huge cycling enthusiast, Clive was determined not to let his diagnosis stop him from pushing himself to his limits. In May 2025, Clive and four of his friends and fellow veterans set off to ride the 3200km Tour de France route, following the 1955 Tour de France course and retracing the tracks of the first British team to compete in the race. Clive spent 18 months planning his dream ride, carefully scheduling it around the regular intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) infusions he receives every six weeks. Made from donated plasma, these infusions help Clive maintain his grip strength, coordination and mobility; without them, this remarkable journey would not have been possible. Clive's journey has been captured on film in No One Rides Alone, an inspiring story with lessons for us all, whatever challenges we face. The film aims to raise awareness of MMN, inspire the rare disease community, and raise funds for MMN research. There are still tickets available for the Auckland screening of the film on Tuesday 14 July at the Capitol Cinema. Find out more about the film & get your tickets via the link below.

    Every year, we work with New Zealand Blood Service to transport life-saving blood and plasma across Aotearoa, helping reach those who need it most. That’s why we’re supporting National Blood Donor Week (8–14 June) through deliveries and our teams’ own donations. NZ Blood's Premium Business Manager, Matt Wenlock, considers himself a cheerleader for blood donations. Since running his first blood drive during National Blood Donor Week 2025, he’s been championing the cause ever since. The most recent event Matt held was just last month, where 60 donations were collected – with the potential to save 180 lives. "Blood drives make it easy and convenient for our people to donate.” says Matt. You can help too by encouraging your teams to donate. One donation can save up to three lives. Find out more here: https://lnkd.in/e_SNcwpc #NBDW26

    More than 700 donations and counting 🩸❤️    For National Blood Donor Week, we’d like to recognise the Vector Limited people who have quietly given their time to donate blood and plasma over the years. Since 2018, our people have made more than 700 donations through New Zealand Blood Service, with an estimated 1,315 lives saved.   Their efforts paused during Covid, then picked up again in 2022. Since then, members of our team have made more than 200 blood or plasma donations.  This is a thank you to everyone who has given their blood or plasma and helped save lives ❤️ Thanks also to Gokul Gnaneswaran, Angela Doone, Sheryl Hickey, Libbie Grey, Ilya Blinov and Craig Turner for sharing these moments. #NationalBloodDonorWeek #BloodDonation #VectorLimited #NewZealandBloodService #CommunityCare #Auckland

    “Starting a Team Red has been one of the best things we've done as a team.”🩸 Not long after the opening of the Amazon Web Services (AWS) data centre in Auckland last year, the office's infrastructure team decided to start donating blood together as part of NZ Blood's "Team Red" group giving programme. One of the team's co-captains, Albert, says donating blood as a group at the Epsom Donor Centre has been a great excuse to step away from the day-to-day, have a laugh, and really get to know each other. "Everyone's got a story, and it's cool to hear them. It's definitely brought us closer.” Since starting their group donations last year, the team has been on a roll, booking appointments up to a year in advance. They’re keenly passionate about getting as many people involved as possible and have already recruited some first-time donors. On a personal level, Albert says donating is a way of giving back to the community that has given him so much since he moved to New Zealand from the Philippines 11 years ago. “New Zealand has been incredibly good to me. Giving blood just feels like a simple but real way to give something back.”
